articles.title: Beyond Right and Wrong: Evaluating Second-order Social Reasoning in Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.05437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Previous AI alignment efforts have focused primarily on first-order social norms -- teaching models what is socially acceptable or unacceptable (e.g., `do not steal'). However, social intelligence depends not only on norm recognition, but also on anticipating who will enforce it and how (e.g., public shame or even imprisonment). articles.title: CriticGen: Generation-Aware Evaluation as Actionable Feedback
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.05439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current evaluation methods for large language models are coarse-grained and decoupled from generation, producing generic explanations that fail to provide actionable feedback for model improvement. We propose CriticGen, a fine-grained, generation-aware evaluation framework that turns evaluation into actionable control for answer improvement. articles.title: When Does Memory Help? A Cost-Aware Evaluation of Long-Term Memory in Tool-Using LLM Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.05441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory for LLM agents is evaluated today by conversational recall benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval), which measure question answering over dialogue history, not whether remembered facts change what a tool-using agent does. articles.summary: arXiv:2609.05446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce AutoFyn, an agent harness inspired by the Expert Iteration algorithm, adapting a frozen model across many rounds by updating persistent state from verified reward signals rather than model weights. articles.title: Damage-Aware Bandit Pruning for Vision and Language Transformers
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.05448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structured post-training pruning of transformers requires selecting complete functional units whose suppression causes limited degradation.
